title: Wolff's law: trabeculae and cortical wall thickness follow stress and bending moment
look_for_in_this_kingdom: CT scans of dinosaur, synapsid and hominin trabecular and cortical bone, fossil bone histology, fossil femur cross-sections
variables_needed: trabecular orientation or fabric tensor per bone region
cortical wall thickness along the shaft

claims.label: Trabeculae of cancellous bone follow the lines of compressive and tensile stress
claims.statement: The trabeculae of cancellous bone, as in the head of the femur, are arranged along the principal lines of compressive and tensile stress of the loaded bone, crossing one another at right angles, exactly as in the engineer's stress diagram of a comparable structure such as a crane-head.
claims.quote: and we have no difficulty in seeing that the anatomical arrangement of the trabeculae follows precisely the mechanical distribution of compressive and tensile stress or, in other words, accords perfectly with the theoretical stress-diagram of the crane.

claims.label: Femoral wall thickness follows the bending-moment distribution along the shaft
claims.statement: Because bending strain is greatest at mid-length of a bent column, the walls of a long bone such as the femur are thickest in the middle of the shaft and thin gradually towards the ends, so that wall thickness forms a graph of the bending moments along the bone.
claims.quote: Hence, if our cylindrical column be exposed to strong bending stresses, it will be prudent and economical to make its walls thickest in the middle and thinning off gradually towards the ends; and if we look at a longitudinal section of a thigh-bone, we shall see that this is just what nature has done.

other_kingdoms_hint.plants: stem and trunk wood grain or reaction wood following mechanical stress, thigmomorphogenesis, tree-ring and fibre-orientation datasets; say plainly when thin
other_kingdoms_hint.animals: micro-CT of femora, humeri and vertebrae across species (MorphoSource, Dryad, Zenodo), trabecular-orientation and bone-ecology databases, finite-element comparisons
